source.title: The Extra Row
source.text:
The Extra Row

Mateo measured straight garden rows for the neighborhood planting day. When Mrs. Green asked whether the new family next door could use the extra row beside his tomatoes, Mateo shook his head. He had planned to fill it with peppers, although he already had more seedlings than his yard could hold.

That night, hard rain washed the neighbors’ newly planted seedlings from their sloped bed. The next morning, Mateo found Ana gathering broken stems. He looked at his untouched extra row, then carried over a tray of pepper seedlings. “We can plant these together,” he said.

Ana and Mateo rebuilt the row, pressed soil around each plant, and shared the watering job. A week later, Ana brought stakes that kept Mateo’s tomato vines upright. Their two families began trading garden tasks and vegetables.

cards.title: State a Theme as a Message
concepts: A theme is a complete message that applies beyond one story.
“Generosity strengthens a community” is a theme; “gardening” is only a topic.
State the message without using a character’s name.
Support: Read one source section at a time. Underline the words named in the question before choosing.

cards.title: Gather Key Details
concepts: Strong theme evidence includes repeated choices, turning points, and consequences.
Mateo shares the extra row; later Ana’s stakes help his tomatoes.
Choose details that show both the message and its result.
Response frame: The source says ____. This supports ____ because ____.

cards.title: Explain How the Theme Develops
concepts: Explain development as a chain: early attitude → key choice → consequence → message.
Mateo guards the row, sees Ana’s loss, shares, and receives cooperation.
An explanation needs evidence and reasoning, not a device label.
Stretch: Compare a second detail and explain whether it strengthens, limits, or changes your first answer.
